title: Allometry and resolution of bee eyes (Apoidea)
why: Would let the view set sharpness from body size, so small sweat bees and large carpenter bees each get their own blur.

authors: Peitsch D, Fietz A, Hertel H, de Souza J, Ventura DF, Menzel R
title: The spectral input systems of hymenopteran insects and their receptor-based colour vision
why: Primary source of receptor peaks for 43 species including wasps and sawflies; would settle which sawflies lack blue and which see red, and so the sawfly colour setting.

title: The angular range of achromatic target detection by honey bees
why: Gives the 5 to 15 degree window of the green-contrast channel that shapes the proposed outline layer; the review numbers would be confirmed or corrected.

title: Temporal resolution of colour vision in the honeybee
why: Would set how slowly the proposed colour wash should follow movement, since bees' colour channels are slower than their green channel.

authors: Ryan LA, Cunningham R, Hart NS, Ogawa Y
title: The buzz around spatial resolving power and contrast sensitivity in the honeybee, Apis mellifera
why: Honeybee resolving power by pattern electroretinogram (0.54 cycles per degree, known here only through Penmetcha et al. 2025) with the full contrast-sensitivity curve; the curve would set the contrast floor (effect 8) band by band, and the paper discusses why retinal and behavioural acuity differ, the fork behind the sharpness row.

title: Spatial acuity of honeybee vision and its spectral properties
why: Original of the 0.26 cycles per degree figure behind the corrected sharpness; would confirm the value and its light level.

title: Temporal acuity of honeybee vision: behavioural studies using moving stimuli
why: Full conditions behind the 200 Hz figure and its fall in dim light; would set the light-dependent pace exactly.

title: Visual field size, binocular domain and the ommatidial array of the compound eyes in worker honey bees
why: Would confirm the 312 degree field and the size of the blind wedge, read here only through Taylor et al. 2019.

title: Achromatic vision in the honeybee at low light intensities
why: Would say what happens to bee colour in dim light, for a dim-light rule in the view.

authors: Warrant EJ, Kelber A, Wallén R, Wcislo WT
title: Ocellar optics in nocturnal and diurnal bees and wasps
why: Ocellar optics across bees and wasps, for the wasp view's row on the small eyes on top of the head.

authors: Zeil J, Ribi WA, Narendra A
title: Polarisation vision in ants, bees and wasps
journal: In: Polarized Light and Polarization Vision in Animal Sciences (Springer)
why: Nothing on polarization in wasps is logged; this chapter would back or remove a sky-compass row for the wasp view.

authors: Jernigan CM, Stafstrom JA, Zaba NC, Vogt CC, Sheehan MJ
title: Color is necessary for face discrimination in the Northern paper wasp, Polistes fuscatus
why: The abstract (logged) says colour is necessary for face discrimination; the full text would give the face sizes and distances used, which would turn the Faces row's 'a few centimetres' into a measured distance.

authors: Sheehan MJ, Jinn J, Tibbetts EA
title: Coevolution of visual signals and eye morphology in Polistes paper wasps
why: Facet sizes for 19 Polistes species could give Florida's paper wasps their own sharpness; only the abstract was read.

title: Dorsoventral asymmetry in the visual field of the bee, Apis mellifica
why: Would test whether the lower visual field matters more, which the downward shift of the sharp zone assumes.

title: A method of estimating the minimum visual stimulus that evokes a behavioural response in the drone, Apis mellifera male
why: Would settle whether drones pursue targets of 0.32 degrees (Land 1997) or 0.41 degrees (Rigosi et al. 2017); citation from Land 1997's reference list, no DOI seen.

title: Structure and function of the larval eye of the sawfly, Perga
why: The sawfly larval eye studied in detail (single-chamber, from fused ommatidia, per Buschbeck 2014); it would show whether a setting for sawfly larvae could be drawn.
